study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Jing et al., Human Brain Mapping, 2023
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Heterogeneous brain dynamic functional connectivity patterns in first-episode drug-naive patients with major depressive disorder

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study used second-order polynomial regression for normative modeling. The normative model was built using second-order polynomial regression to model the relationship between age and 40 brain network features (20 IC measures and 20 fluctuation coefficients). Z-scores were calculated based on the 5th, 50th, and 95th percentiles from bootstrapping confidence intervals. 10-fold cross-validation was applied to build an aggregation normative model.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: we built the second-order polynomial regression normative model (see supplementary materials) on the relationship between age and these 40 features, respectively. We estimated the 50th (median) percentile with bootstrapping confidence intervals to quantify the extent of deviations for any FEDN-MDD patient from the normative model.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Jing2023.pdf.md: Section 2.3 Normative modeling and estimation of the feature deviations

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: The study modeled dynamic functional connectivity patterns derived from resting-state fMRI. Specifically, 20 independent component (IC) measures (global efficiency coefficient of each IC) and 20 fluctuation coefficients (average change of frame-wise variation of each IC's time-varying weights) were computed using group information guided independent component analysis (GIG-ICA) on dynamic functional connectivity matrices calculated via sliding time window method (window length = 60s, step size = 1) based on 90 ROIs from the AAL atlas.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: For each subject, we computed whole-brain dynamic functional connectivity matrices based on m (m = 90) ROIs from the automated anatomical labeling (AAL) template using a sliding time window method (window length = 60s, step size = 1). ... Finally, the dynamic functional connectivity pattern of each subject was represented by 20 IC measures (global efficiency coefficient of each IC) and 20 fluctuation coefficients (average change of the frame-wise variation of each IC's time-varying weights)
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Jing2023.pdf.md: Section 2.2 Dynamic functional connectivity pattern and feature extraction

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The normative model used age as the sole explanatory variable. The second-order polynomial regression normative model was built on the relationship between age and the 40 brain network features. The z-score formula shows that predictions were made for each feature at a given age. Age was modeled with a second-order polynomial term (Age and Age^2 implicitly included).
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: we built the second-order polynomial regression normative model (see supplementary materials) on the relationship between age and these 40 features, respectively. ... For individuals with index i, z_ijf was the normalized deviation value for feature f of IC j. C:real was the real value of the feature, and C:5th, C:50th and C:95th were the predictions in 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles for the same age respectively.
